The reads of sdata[0] after blockReduce are ordered by the trailing __syncthreads() at L63; the inter-step barriers L59/L60 order the first two block-level steps (threads 128..255, 64..127) before warpReduce; only the six warp-synchronous steps race.

class_reason: warpReduce takes `volatile float *sdata`, so every access of the pair is a volatile (strong) shared access (verify.strong_accesses: both). By D20 a pair is SC when BOTH accesses are strong: the unordered volatile-store / volatile-load conflict between adjacent steps is an SC pair, not a DR (no plain access is involved). Intra-warp, no __syncwarp: a formal ITS-style conflict that is benign in practice because the warp stays converged.
buggy_expected: SC (unordered strong conflict), intra-warp, for each adjacent step pair of warpReduce in warp 0 of every block (L46/L47, L47/L48, L48/L49, L49/L50, L50/L51); a detector that treats volatile as atomic-like will not report it, one that follows happens-before with no __syncwarp will report it as SC

D20 caveat: volatile accesses to SHARED memory may lower to plain LDS/STS on sm_89 (no .STRONG qualifier in SASS); the SASS-level strength would then look plain and a detector reading strength from SASS would report these pairs as DR instead of SC. To be checked with cuobjdump -sass when the target is built; the oracle's SC follows the source-level volatile (record: expected_class SC, not DR).

warpReduce / blockReduce are non-inline __device__ functions with a volatile pointer parameter; the compiler may inline them into each caller kernel, giving one copy per call site (frame_distance_kernel has three).
In frame_distance_kernel the `accum`, `valid` and `total` arrays are zero-initialised by each thread at L570-L572 before the loop; the pair concerns only the reduction steps.

upstream_status.dispute_points: (1) Accesses are volatile, which PTX treats as strong/relaxed-like; a detector that treats volatile as atomic-like will not flag it, while one following HB ordering (no syncwarp => no order) will. (2) In practice nvcc keeps the warp converged here so results are correct on sm_70..sm_90; NVIDIA's own guidance (CUDA 9 'Using CUDA Warp-Level Primitives') says this idiom is formally invalid on Volta+. (3) Maintainers have not touched it; unlikely to be accepted as a bug by the project itself.
